Not quite. Operations regarding the distribution of a schedule A controlled substance, even if it is distributed legally, must be reported as such. All advertising and selling expenses resulting from the legal distribution of a schedule A substance are not tax deductible.

Schedule A (itemized deductions) is irrelevant to this conversation. We're not talking about what deductions they've claimed. We're talking about whether they have to itemize their sales, which they don't under most circumstances.

Well, not just schedule A. Anything listed on schedules I and II.

https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/280E

The IRS treats dispensary expenses as the legal trafficking of a controlled substance, and uses code 280E to make expenses non-deductible.
Schedule A (tax deductions) and Schedule I and II (controlled substance lists) are two different things.

You report your income from operations as normal, but with a huge caveat. Any operations for the distribution of a schedule A substance, which includes both selling and advertising expense, are not deductible at the federal level. As this can be a significant portion of the business' income (including employee wages, COGS, rental expense, and more), it makes it difficult to be profitable.
